title: Handing a closure to transaction
summary: E0597 from a caller-chosen lifetime, a move to HRTB, E0507 once retries force FnMut, and a landing on BoxFuture.

turns.user: i keep hand writing begin, commit on success, rollback on failure. i want db.transaction(|tx| ...) instead

assistant.body: Certainly. Db gets a transaction method. It takes the closure as FnOnce, commits on Ok and rolls back on Err. Tx holds a &mut Conn, so one lifetime 'a lines the closure argument up with the borrow of self, and cleanup then runs on every path.

turns.user: this doesn't even cargo check. E0597, `tx` does not live long enough

assistant.body: Apologies, my signature let the caller pick 'a. The 'a in the &'a mut Tx<'a> that f demands is chosen outside the function, so the local tx built inside it is too short lived, and that is the E0597. What is needed is a lifetime the callee picks fresh per call, a higher ranked bound. for<'a> FnOnce(&'a mut Tx<'a>) does not work either: behind a &mut nothing is variant, so Tx<'a> never unifies with the real Tx<'_>. The two lifetimes stay separate.
sed -i '' "s/transaction<'a, T, F>(&'a mut self/transaction<T, F>(\&mut self/; s/FnOnce(&'a mut Tx<'a>)/for<'a, 'b> FnOnce(\&'a mut Tx<'b>)/" src/db.rs

turns.user: builds. now one more thing, retry up to 3 times when it comes back Conflict

assistant.body: Retrying means calling f more than once, which FnOnce cannot do, so it goes up to FnMut first. An & is literal on the pattern side, but on the replacement side it stands for the whole match, so that one gets a backslash.
sed -i '' "s/mut self, f: F)/mut self, mut f: F)/; s/FnOnce(&'a mut Tx<'b>)/FnMut(\&'a mut Tx<'b>)/" src/db.rs

turns.user: retries work. but moving seed onto transaction gives me E0507, cannot move out of `name`, a captured variable in an `FnMut` closure

assistant.body: Right. An FnMut closure may run more than once, so its body cannot move a captured String out, and that is the E0507. insert_sql takes &str and the call site passes &name. name.clone() would also compile, but it allocates on every retry.

turns.user: sorry, one last one. all of this needs to be async, we're on sqlx now

assistant.body: Async closures are not stable yet, so the closure returns a BoxFuture instead. The future it hands back still borrows the &mut Tx, so that borrow's lifetime has to appear in the future's own type: with BoxFuture<'a, ...>, 'a is picked per call. sqlx's Pool::transaction has nearly the same shape. Call sites have to wrap the body in Box::pin(async move { ... }).
